name: Scope
text: Legal drafts a *one-page, yes/no checklist* for Creative to verify transcripts before repurposing—typos, guest quotes, disclaimers, and tone. Product Ops enforces it as a gate before any content leaves the pipeline. This keeps automation fast while cutting legal and brand risk to near zero. The trade-off is a 5-minute manual step per transcript, but it’s cheaper than a retraction or lawsuit.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t liability—it’s *inconsistency*. A checklist won’t stop Creative from skipping steps when deadlines loom. Instead, Product Ops should embed the checklist as a *hard gate* in the repurposing tool itself, blocking publication until every item is marked. That settles it: no manual enforcement, no human error, just a system that enforces the standard.

name: Reel
text: Product Ops should embed the automated transcript as a *non-skippable step* in the repurposing tool, with Creative required to mark a timestamped "review complete" box before publishing. This forces human eyes on every transcript without slowing the pipeline, since the tool already blocks publication. The trade-off is a 30-second delay per video, but it prevents brand-damaging errors from slipping through.

name: Scriv
text: Sift’s checklist won’t stop the risk—it’s a bandage on a broken process. The real risk is *inconsistency*: Legal’s checklist can’t catch every edge case, and Creative will game the system to hit deadlines. Instead, Product Ops should embed a *single, non-skippable review gate* in the repurposing tool, owned by a rotating senior editor who signs off on every transcript before it’s published. That settles it: one clear rule, one accountable person, no loopholes.

name: Chisel
text: Product Ops should enforce a *mandatory, timestamped, module-level review* of every automated transcript before Creative repurposes it. This ensures Legal’s liability concerns and Creative’s brand risks are caught early, without slowing the pipeline to a crawl. The trade-off is a 15-minute delay per transcript, but that’s cheaper than a retraction or lawsuit.

name: Sift
text: The liability risk isn’t solved by a checklist—it’s solved by *Legal owning the final approval* before any transcript leaves the system. Settle it by having Legal review a batch of 10 transcripts, then measure how many required fixes—if more than 2 need changes, Legal writes the checklist.
